### Properties

- `last_system: String`: The last prompts built (tests read them; never saved, logged or printed).
- `recent_of: Callable`: Optional: func(resident_id: String) -> Array[String], the resident's last chat lines (talk prompt).
- `live_down: bool`: True after DOWN_AFTER failed live calls in a row, until a call succeeds (live_changed).

### Functions

- `func setup(p_sim: CitySim, p_people: Residents, p_client: GmiClient, p_brain: CityBrain, p_directory: CityDirectory) -> void`: Wires the minds to the city. client may be offline (live_enabled false): then no call is made.
- `func busy(kind: String) -> bool`: True while a call of this kind ("round", "player" or "talk") is in flight.
- `func live() -> bool`: True when calls go to the network (offline gates: always false).
- `func reset() -> void`: Forgets per-city state (load, New City) and live_down; the LRU and stats survive.
- `func run_round(topic: Dictionary, recent: Array) -> Array`: One batched round: 4-8 lines from 4-6 picked residents (and maybe a mayor) about a topic. Coroutine; returns validated lines [{"id", "author", "role", "district", "text", "reply_to", "reply_idx"}] (reply_to is a shown seq from recent, reply_idx an earlier line of this round).
- `func run_mayors_round(recent: Array) -> Array`: A round of the rival mayors arguing in the chat while nobody lives in the city yet: 3-5 lines from 2-3 mayors. Coroutine; live only ([] offline, while a round is out or when the call fails).
- `func reply_to_player(text: String, district: int, recent: Array) -> Array`: Replies to a player chat line (2-4 residents, district-weighted). A mayor the line names (or, for a bare "mayor", the district's) answers first, about their own last turn. text may hold several coalesced lines joined by "\n". Each reply gets its own seed, so a question asked twice gets new words. Coroutine; same line dicts as run_round (reply_to -1: the caller points them at the player's message).
- `func talk(r: Dictionary, turns: Array, player_text: String) -> Dictionary`: One face-to-face reply from resident r: {"reply", "mood_delta", "memory", "emote", "source"}. turns: earlier lines [{"who": "you"|"them", "text"}]. Coroutine: one live call when online (falls back to the LRU, then talk_busy), the heuristic offline.
- `func talk_busy(r: Dictionary, said: String = "") -> Dictionary`: What r says when the live reply failed or is late (source "busy"): an honest line in their world instead of a made-up answer. No mood change and nothing to remember.
- `func talk_user(r: Dictionary, turns: Array, said: String) -> String`: The talk prompt's user JSON: the resident's card with directory names instead of coordinates, state, plan, thought, mood reason, last 8 memories, what is nearby, the city facts of their district, their last 3 chat lines, the last 6 turns and player_line (the only place the player's text appears).
- `func validate_talk(data: Dictionary) -> Dictionary`: Validates a talk reply: reply <= 40 words (debranded, no URL, no model name), mood_delta in -1..1, memory <= 15 words, emote whitelisted. {} when the reply is unusable.
- `func greeting(r: Dictionary) -> String`: The first thing r says when the player walks up: their own "say" line, else a greeting in their voice.
- `func greeting_emote(r: Dictionary) -> String`: The emote that goes with r's greeting: a wave from friendly voices, a frown when miserable.
- `func talk_heuristic(r: Dictionary, turns: Array, said: String) -> Dictionary`: Deterministic offline reply in r's voice (C §4 "Offline"): answers the quick questions from the resident's real state and keywords in free text from their job, home and the city.
- `func pick_participants(topic: Dictionary, k: int, rng: RandomNumberGenerator, must: Array = []) -> Array[Dictionary]`: Picks k residents for topic, weighted by proximity to the topic tile (or the player's district), matching skills for incidents, sociable / outspoken traits (shy down) and extreme moods. must: resident ids that join first (named in a player line).
- `func chat_card(r: Dictionary) -> Dictionary`: The compact prompt card of a chat participant: id, name, job, traits, mood, mood reason, the last 2 memories, home and work as directory names (never coordinates).
- `func clean_card(c: Dictionary) -> Dictionary`: resident.card() with every coordinate replaced by directory names (talk prompts).
- `func topic_facts(topic: Dictionary) -> Dictionary`: Topic facts for prompts (names only, never coordinates).
- `func validate_lines(data: Dictionary, picked: Array, mayor: int, recent: Array, more_mayors: Array = []) -> Array`: Validates model lines (C §3): ids must be picked (or "m<k>" for mayor and more_mayors), text trimmed to 140 and debranded; empty lines, URLs, model names and more than 2 sentences are dropped; at most 8.
- `func heuristic_round(topic: Dictionary, picked: Array, mayor: int, recent: Array, rng: RandomNumberGenerator) -> Array`: Deterministic offline round: an opener on the topic from the first participant, then reactions, agreements and disagreements in each participant's voice, threaded by reply_idx.
- `func heuristic_player(said: String, picked: Array, rng: RandomNumberGenerator, city: Dictionary = {}, mi: int = -1) -> Array`: Deterministic offline replies to the player's line, by what the line is about. The first resident quotes the city fact the line asks about (CITY_ABOUT, from city: ChatFacts.build for the player's district; now and then for small talk too) and mayor mi, when the line names one, answers first from their own last turn.
- `static func intent_of(text: String) -> String`: Coarse intent of a player line: greet, how, around, mayor, bye, power, water, traffic, money, jobs, incident, crime, food, fun, news, who, help or generic.
- `static func voice(r: Dictionary) -> String`: A resident's voice: grump, worried, sunny, civic or plain (traits first, then mood).
- `func facts(r: Dictionary, topic: Dictionary = {}) -> Dictionary`: Template tokens for r: first, name, job, district, street, work, mayor, mayor_last, place, ev, ev_cap, what, headline, label, tax (and the topic's when given).
- `func lru_get(key: String) -> Variant`: The cached live answer for key, or null.
- `func lru_put(key: String, value: Variant) -> void`: Stores a live answer (never saved, never flushed, never written through GmiClient).
- `func lru_size() -> int`: Entries in the LRU.
- `static func mayor_panel(lead: int, n: int, rng: RandomNumberGenerator) -> Array[int]`: n distinct mayor indices: lead first when it is one (else one by rng), then rivals by rng.

## `scripts/ai/city_brain.gd`

class_name `CityBrain` · extends `"res://scripts/ai/brain_calls.gd"`

Puts GMI model inference on every layer of the city. Each in-game day it batches: - 5 AI mayors (different models) that read their district map and issue build/zone/tax actions - Citizen Voices: sampled residents describe their lives; complaints feed back to mayors - GridFall Gazette: a news editor writes the day's headline from real events - Chaos Director: picks disasters that probe the city's weaknesses - Grid Operator: sets load-shedding priority when power or water runs short - Council Speaker: rules on ordinance proposals using the mayors' votes plus an on-demand Street Inspector that role-plays whatever tile the player clicks. Live calls fall back to the recorded replay cache, then to local heuristics.

### Signals

- `mayor_thinking(mi: int)`
- `mayor_decided(mi: int, decision: Dictionary)`
- `citizens_spoke(voices: Array)`
- `news_published(paper: Dictionary)`
- `council_ruled(ruling: Dictionary)`
- `chaos_decided(decision: Dictionary)`
- `operator_decided(decision: Dictionary)`
- `inspector_answered(report: Dictionary)`

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `MayorTurns = preload("res://scripts/ai/mayor_turns.gd")`
- `BrainText = preload("res://scripts/ai/brain_text.gd")`
- `RoadPlans = preload("res://scripts/ai/road_plans.gd")`
- `MayorPrompts = preload("res://scripts/ai/mayor_prompts.gd")`
- `MayorContext = preload("res://scripts/ai/mayor_context.gd")`
- `CouncilLog = preload("res://scripts/ai/council_log.gd")`
- `MAX_WAIT_MS = 75000`

### Properties

- `council_history: Array[Dictionary]`: The council's last CouncilLog.KEEP rulings, newest last, and the notes mayors left each other (mayor id -> [{from, day, kind, text, amount, seen}]; MayorContext, flag mayor_context_v2).
- `stagger_mayors: bool`: Street mode sets this: the mayors take the day's turns one by one through the day (turns), so a player on foot sees decisions land every few minutes. Off (orbit, tests): all at dawn.

### Functions

- `func setup(p_sim: CitySim, p_client: GmiClient) -> void`
- `func send_decree(text: String) -> void`
- `func spread_pending() -> bool`: True while the day round still has pieces waiting for a frame (the sim's spread gate).
- `func drain_step() -> void`: Runs the round's next waiting piece (one a frame; the drain scheduler calls it for more).
- `func day_of_sim() -> int`
- `func residents_spoke(_day: int) -> void`: With AI residents, the voices the mayors hear are the residents' own words from today's plans.
- `func inspect_tile(x: int, y: int) -> void`
- `func to_dict() -> Dictionary`
- `func from_dict(d: Dictionary) -> void`

## `scripts/ai/council_log.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

The council vote board's data: what the Speaker did with each proposal and how the five mayors had voted. CityBrain._run_council takes a tally of the proposals on the floor before the ruled ones leave it (tally), puts it on the ruling it emits and appends one record per proposal (and per repeal) to brain.council_history (record), the newest KEEP rulings. The Speaker is free to overrule the count (the system prompt lets it pass a proposal with only 2 yes, and nothing forces it to pass one with 3), so every record says whether the outcome matches the vote: "override" is true for an enactment with fewer than MAJORITY yes and for a proposal that stayed out (deferred or rejected) with MAJORITY yes or more. verdict() and score() put that in words for the HUDs ("passed 3-2", "OVERRIDE: passed with 2"). Only a LIVE Speaker is held to the count: a recorded (replay) Speaker did not read today's votes, so its ruling that disagrees with them is not an override (the record says "against" and the words drop the count). Pure data and text, no nodes.

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `KEEP = 20`: Rulings kept in the history and in a save.
- `MAJORITY = 3`: Yes votes (of five) that make a majority.
- `OUTCOMES = ["enacted", "rejected", "deferred", "repealed"]`
- `PASSIVE = { "enacted": "passed", "rejected": "rejected", "deferred": "deferred", "repealed": "rep...`

### Functions

- `static func tally(proposals: Dictionary, enacted: Array, rejected: Array, source: String = "live") -> Array[Dictiona`: The proposals on the floor with their votes, each classed by what the Speaker did: [{"key", "by" (display name), "by_id", "votes" {mayor id: "yes"|"no"}, "notes" {mayor id: reason}, "yes", "no", "outcome" (enacted|rejected|deferred), "override"}]. Call it before the ruled proposals are erased from proposals.
- `static func goes_against(outcome: String, yes: int) -> bool`: Whether an outcome disagrees with a count of yes votes, whoever ruled.
- `static func is_override(outcome: String, yes: int, source: String = "live") -> b`: Whether the Speaker went against the count: it disagrees AND the Speaker is a live model that read today's votes (source "live"); a replayed or scripted ruling is never an override.
- `static func record(brain: CityBrain, ruling: Dictionary) -> void`: Appends the ruling's records to brain.council_history (newest last, KEEP at most) and, with mayor context v2 on, tells the Gazette's feed when the Speaker went against the vote.
- `static func score(e: Dictionary) -> String`: "3-2" (yes-no) for a record, "" for one with no votes (a repeal).
- `static func verdict(e: Variant) -> String`: What the Speaker did, against the count: "passed 3-2", "deferred 2-1", "OVERRIDE: passed with 2", "OVERRIDE: deferred with 4 yes", "repealed".
- `static func quiet(e: Dictionary) -> bool`: Whether a record's ruling disagrees with its count without being an override (a replayed Speaker): its words leave the count out rather than set a ruling beside votes it never saw.
- `static func seats(e: Dictionary) -> Dictionary`: Mayors' first names split by how they voted: {"yes": [..], "no": [..], "none": [..]} in seat order, for a record (or any dictionary with "votes").
- `static func first_name(display: String) -> String`
- `static func last_for(history: Array, key: String) -> Dictionary`: The newest record for a proposal key, or {}.
- `static func restore(raw: Variant) -> Array[Dictionary]`: A saved history made safe to load: dictionaries only, known outcomes, votes and notes cut to the five mayors, text de-branded and cut again, the newest KEEP.
- `static func cut(t: String, n: int) -> String`: t cut to at most n characters at a word boundary, with "..." where something was left out (plain dots: web builds have no system fonts, so a missing glyph would show as a box).

## `scripts/ai/gmi_admission.gd`

class_name `GmiAdmission` · extends `RefCounted`

How many live calls GmiClient has out at once, with the mayors first. A browser keeps few connections per host (six over HTTP/1.1) and a key's tier may rate-limit a burst, while at dawn ten resident batches, the chatter and five mayors all go out together. With the cap on, the background roles (the residents, the street chatter, the talk) wait for a free slot instead of all going out at once; the roles that are the city's own business (the mayors, the support agents and the "Ask the five" panel) never wait, and while one of them is in flight the background gets half the slots. A call still waiting when its own timeout is up gives up and the caller falls back as for any failed call. Off by default (flag gmi_inflight_cap): it paces the minds, and the right numbers depend on the key's tier, which no test can know. GmiClient asks can_enter() and brackets a call with enter() and leave().

### Constants

- `PRIORITY_ROLES = [ "mayor", "news", "council", "chaos", "citizens", "operator", "inspector", "arena" ]`: Roles that never wait for a slot.
- `BACKGROUND_MAX = 6`: Background calls allowed at once (halved, at least 1, while a priority call is out).

### Functions

- `static func is_priority(role: String) -> bool`
- `func slots() -> int`: Background slots free right now: background_max, or half of it while a priority call is out.
- `func can_enter(role: String) -> bool`: True when a call of this role may go out now. A priority call always may.
- `func enter(role: String) -> void`
- `func leave(role: String) -> void`
- `func background() -> int`: Background calls out now (the tests read it).
- `func priority() -> int`: Priority calls out now.

## `scripts/ai/gmi_breakers.gd`

class_name `GmiBreakers` · extends `RefCounted`

The circuit breakers of GmiClient, one per group of roles. A single breaker for every call let a burst of failing background calls (ten parallel resident batches meeting a 429, a chatter round timing out) open the circuit for the mayors too, who then played their turn from the replay cache for 30 s. Each group now counts its own consecutive service failures and opens alone; the mayors, the support agents (Gazette, council, chaos, citizens, operator, inspector), the residents and the rest each have theirs. The group "chat" is the default: every role not named in GROUPS (the street chatter, the face-to-face talk, anything added later) lands in it, and its breaker is the one GmiClient keeps as `breaker`. state() is the aggregate the alerts and the street badge read: "open" when any group is open, else "half_open" when any is probing, else "closed".

### Signals

- `changed(group: String, from: String, to: String)`: One group's breaker moved (group, from, to).

### Constants

- `DEFAULT_GROUP = "chat"`
- `GROUPS = { "mayor": "mayor", "news": "support", "council": "support", "chaos": "support", "citiz...`: The role -> group table. Roles missing here belong to DEFAULT_GROUP.

### Functions

- `static func group_of(role: String) -> String`: The group a role's calls are counted in.
- `func breaker_for(role: String) -> CircuitBreaker`: The breaker of the group role belongs to.
- `func group(name: String) -> CircuitBreaker`: The breaker of a group (made on first use).
- `func state(now_ms: int = -1) -> String`: "open" when any group is open (peeked: an open breaker past its cool-down reads half_open), else "half_open" when any is, else "closed".
- `func mayor_state(now_ms: int = -1) -> String`: The mayors' group alone (peeked): what says whether the city's own minds are reachable. The street badge and Ask the five read this, so a residents or chatter storm does not mark the mayors as down.
- `func states(now_ms: int = -1) -> Dictionary`: {group: state} for every group seen so far (peeked).
- `func tripped(now_ms: int = -1) -> PackedStringArray`: The names of the groups that are not closed, sorted ("" when all are closed).
- `func reset() -> void`: Closes every group's breaker.

## `scripts/ai/gmi_cache.gd`

class_name `GmiCache` · extends `RefCounted`

The shape of GmiClient's answer caches: {key: [{day, data}, ...]}. Pure functions over those dictionaries, kept apart from the client (a node that is already near the file-size cap) so the lookup rule and the save diet have one place and a test can run them without a node. Lookup: the entry nearest the asked day wins (the earlier day on a tie). The recorded replay cache has a horizon: it holds one captured game, so past the last day recorded for a key its entries are no longer an answer to the day asked (a day-14 city must not replay day 12 forever) and the caller falls through to the scripted planner. The session cache (this run's own live answers) has no horizon: it is the freshest thing there is. Save diet: a save keeps each key's last SAVE_KEEP_DAYS distinct days (the lookup reads the nearest day, so older ones are never the answer once newer ones exist). The in-memory cache is not touched.

### Constants

- `SAVE_KEEP_DAYS = 3`: Distinct days per key a save (and the session file) keeps.

### Functions

- `static func last_day(entries: Array) -> int`: The last day any entry of entries records, or -1 when none does.
- `static func nearest(entries: Array, day: int, horizon: bool = false) -> Dictionary`: The data of the entry of entries nearest day, or {} when there is none. horizon true: {} too when day is past the last day the entries record.
- `static func lookup(session: Dictionary, replay: Dictionary, key: String, day: int, horizon: bool) -> Dictionary`: The answer for key on day: the session cache's nearest entry, else the replay cache's (inside its horizon when horizon is true), else {}.
- `static func pruned(cache: Dictionary, keep: int = SAVE_KEEP_DAYS) -> Dictionary`: A copy of cache keeping, for each key, the entries of its last keep distinct days (in their original order). The entries themselves are shared with cache, not copied.
- `static func entry_count(cache: Dictionary) -> int`: How many entries cache holds in all (the flush signature and the tests use it).
- `static func clear_session(client: GmiClient) -> void`: A new city starts with no answers of the last one and zero counters (the calls in flight stay counted: they land after it): a New City must not replay the old city's live answers.

## `scripts/ai/gmi_client.gd`

class_name `GmiClient` · extends `Node`

Async GMI Cloud chat client with JSON extraction, a recorded replay cache, and heuristic fallback. Every call is logged with its source (live / cache / heuristic).

### Signals

- `call_logged(record: Dictionary)`
- `call_skipped(record: Dictionary)`: A live_json call that never left the process (offline, circuit open, no free slot): it is not in the log, but the ModelLedger counts it so a model that is being skipped shows as such.
- `breaker_changed(state: String)`: The circuit breakers' aggregate moved to state ("closed" / "open" / "half_open"): one group opening while another is already open does not repeat it.

### Constants

- `CHAT_URL = "https://api.gmi-serving.com/v1/chat/completions"`
- `MODELS_URL = "https://api.gmi-serving.com/v1/models"`: The model list the readiness check reads (GET, once per key; see GmiPreflight).
- `PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_S = 12.0`
- `PREFLIGHT_MAX_BODY = 1 << 20`: The model list is read for its ids only: a body past this is cut off by the HTTPRequest.
- `MAX_RETRIES = 2`: Retries after the first attempt, for transient failures only (see is_retryable()).
- `BACKOFF_BASE_MS = 500`
- `BACKOFF_CAP_MS = 4000`
- `LIVE_WINDOW = 20`: Live outcomes kept for the failure-ratio alert.
- `LIVE_BADGE_MIN_OUTCOMES = 3`: Fewest live outcomes in the window before live_failure_ratio() reports anything. The street badge turns red ("Reconnecting") above 0.5, and one failed call out of one is 1.0: a single stray timeout, one 401 or the first call after boot must not say the link is down. Three is the least that lets "most of them failed" mean something while an outage still shows within a few calls. The ops alert (data/alert_rules.json, gmi_live_failures, min_calls 6) waits for more on purpose: it interrupts the player, the badge only informs.
- `RETRY_RESULTS = [HTTPRequest.RESULT_CANT_CONNECT, HTTPRequest.RESULT_CANT_RESOLVE, HTTPRequest.RESULT_C...`: Network results worth another attempt; TLS, redirect, body-size and file errors are not.
- `RETRY_HTTP = [408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504]`
- `REPLAY_CACHE_PATH = "res://data/gmi_replay_cache.json"`
- `SESSION_CACHE_PATH = "user://gmi_session_cache.json"`
- `WEB_KEY_STORE = "gridfall.gmi_key"`: Browser localStorage names for the player's own key (web build); written only after the player ticks "Remember on this device", read back at boot. Never a log target (Redact owns the key).
- `WEB_KEY_CONSENT = "gridfall.gmi_key.remember"`
- `MAX_LOG = 300`
- `MODEL_EXTRAS = { "deepseek-ai/": {"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}},  "moonshotai/": {"reasoning_effor...`: Hybrid reasoning models spend the whole token budget thinking unless told not to. Keys are model-id prefixes; values are merged into the request body.
- `TEMPERATURE = 0.7`: Sampling temperature of every call, unless the model refused it (temperature_of).
- `ISOLATED_ROLES = ["arena"]`: Roles whose live calls are a side question, not the city's own business (the "Ask the five" panel): they leave the breaker, the live_outcomes window and the live_ok/live_fail counts alone, so five parallel questions that meet a 429 cannot turn the whole city to replay.
- `KEY_TEST_SYSTEM = "Reply with the single word ok."`: The key test (test_key): a tiny prompt, KEY_TEST_TOKENS tokens, one attempt, and a timeout generous enough for a cold model without leaving the player staring at "Testing".
- `KEY_TEST_USER = "ping"`
- `KEY_TEST_TOKENS = 8`
- `KEY_TEST_TIMEOUT_S = 12.0`

### Properties

- `player_key: String`: A key the player typed in the settings (web build or any platform); "" while the boot key (GMI_API_KEY or ~/.factory/settings.json) is the one in use.
- `breaker`: The default group's breaker (the street chatter, the talk and any role not named in GmiBreakers.GROUPS): it opens after 4 consecutive service failures; while open, chat_json goes straight to the cache or heuristic and live_json fails fast with "circuit open". The mayors, the support agents and the residents each have their own in `breakers` (see breakers.breaker_for), so a failing group cannot open the circuit for the others; breaker_state() is the aggregate.
- `admission`: Live calls out now, the mayors first (flag gmi_inflight_cap; see GmiAdmission).
- `preflight`: The readiness check of the key in use (one GET of the model list per key, GmiPreflight). It starts by itself when a key is set, but only where the game runs (preflight.enabled, which Main sets): a test client never reaches for the network.
- `live_outcomes: Array[bool]`: The last LIVE_WINDOW live outcomes (true = ok), oldest first.
- `temperature_of: Dictionary`: Models that refused TEMPERATURE (an HTTP 400 naming the temperature) and get 1.0 instead.
- `web_build: bool`: True in the browser export (_detect_web). An instance variable (not a call in _post) so a test can stand in for the web build; nothing else sets it.
- `sleep_ms`: Test-only hook for the retry backoff's sleep, in milliseconds. Empty in the game, where the retry loop waits on a SceneTree timer; a test assigns a recorder so the backoff contract is checked exactly instead of through frame-timer timing (a SceneTree timer burns frame deltas, so on a loaded runner one stalled frame can end the wait long before its wall-clock delay). Not wired to any flag or environment switch: nothing outside a test ever sets it.

### Functions

- `func has_key() -> bool`
- `func set_player_key(key: String) -> bool`: A key the player typed in the settings ("bring your own key"): replaces the boot key in memory and is registered with the redactor so it can never reach a log. The key stays in this session only (remember_player_key() is what, on the web and only after the player ticks Remember, saves it on their own device). An empty key puts the boot key back in use. Returns has_key().
- `func remember_player_key(key: String) -> void`: Saves this key on the player's own device (web build, after they tick Remember): written straight to the browser's localStorage, never through Godot's files or logs. No-op elsewhere.
- `func has_remembered_key(key: String = "") -> bool`: True when this device holds a remembered key the player asked for (web build only). With key given, true only when the saved copy is that very key (a copy of another key does not count).
- `func forget_remembered_key() -> void`: Drops the Remember tick and the stored key from this device (web build only). The key set with set_player_key stays in memory until cleared or the page closes.
- `func set_live(enabled: bool) -> void`
- `func breaker_state() -> String`: The aggregate of the breakers: "open" when any group's is open, else "half_open" when one is probing (an open breaker past its cool-down reads half_open), else "closed". The alerts and the alerts read this one (the street badge and Ask the five read breakers.mayor_state()).
- `func live_failure_ratio() -> float`: Share of failed live calls among the last LIVE_WINDOW. 0 while fewer than LIVE_BADGE_MIN_OUTCOMES calls have been seen: too few to call it a trend.
- `static func is_retryable(result_code: int, http_code: int) -> bool`: True for failures another attempt may fix: transient network results, 408, 429 and 500/502/503/504.
- `static func is_service_failure(result_code: int, http_code: int) -> bool`: True when the failure says the service (not the request or the reply) is unhealthy; these count toward opening the breaker.
- `static func backoff_ms(attempt: int, jitter01: float) -> int`: Delay before retry number attempt (0-based): exponential from BACKOFF_BASE_MS, capped at BACKOFF_CAP_MS, with "equal jitter" (jitter01 in 0..1 picks a point in the upper half).
- `static func request_headers(key: String, request_id: String, trace_id: String, web: bool) -> PackedStringArray`: The HTTP headers of one chat request. Desktop sends all five. In a browser every header beyond Authorization and Content-Type is a non-safelisted header the preflight must allow, and GMI's CORS answer (measured 2026-11-03: OPTIONS /v1/chat/completions allows Content-Type, Authorization, X-Requested-With and x-gmi-request-id) does not list User-Agent, X-Request-ID or X-Trace-ID, so with them the browser blocks every live call before it leaves. web = true therefore sends only what the preflight allows and needs. The request and trace ids still label the call in the local GMI Log and trace; the web build just cannot put them on the wire.
- `static func web_headers_active(is_web: bool) -> bool`: True when requests must use the web-safe header set: the browser build with the gmi_web_safe_headers flag on (turn it off if GMI's CORS list ever admits the tracing headers).
- `static func key_test_model(models: Array) -> String`: The model the key test asks: among models, the one that looks cheapest by its name (a "lite" id, then a "flash" id, then the first). Offline, names are all there is: no price list is read.
- `static func classify_key_reply(live: Dictionary) -> Dictionary`: The key test's verdict for a _post reply: {"status": "ok" | "rejected" | "rate_limited" | "blocked" | "error", "http": int, "timed_out": bool}. ok is HTTP 200 whatever the body (the key was accepted; the model need not have produced JSON), rejected 401/403, rate_limited 429, blocked a network-level failure with no HTTP answer (in a browser a CORS block and being offline look the same) and error anything else (other HTTP codes, a request that could not be built). timed_out marks the blocked case where the wait ran out instead of the connection failing: a slow or stalled answer is not a CORS block and the panel says so.
- `func chat_json(role: String, agent_id: String, model: String, system_prompt: String, user_prompt: String, day: int, max_tokens: int, timeout_s: float, heuristic: Callable) -> Dictionary`: Returns {ok, data, source, latency_ms, model, error, raw}. Never fails: falls back to the replay cache (same role/agent, nearest day) and then to the heuristic callable.
- `func live_json(role: String, agent_id: String, model: String, system_prompt: String, user_prompt: String, day: int, max_tokens: int, timeout_s: float) -> Dictionary`: Live-only call for callers that cache per item themselves (resident batches). Never touches the role-level cache; on failure returns ok=false so the caller can fall back.
- `func test_refusal() -> String`: Why a key test cannot go out right now: "" when it can, else "no_key", "offline" (GRIDFALL_OFFLINE=1, whose whole meaning is that nothing calls GMI: the same switch _refresh_live honours) or "switched_off" (the gmi_live kill switch).
- `func test_key() -> Dictionary`: One tiny live call that says whether the key in use works: KEY_TEST_TOKENS tokens to the model key_test_model() picks from ResidentMinds.MODELS, through the same _post (so the same headers). It is the player's own explicit request, so it deliberately ignores the Live toggle and an open breaker, and it leaves no trace in the game: not the breaker, live_outcomes, stats, the log, session_cache or the replay cache. Refused (see test_refusal) without a key, under GRIDFALL_OFFLINE=1 or with the gmi_live kill switch off: nothing is sent and "refused" says why. Returns {"status": "ok" | "rejected" | "rate_limited" | "blocked" | "error", "seconds": float, "http": int, "timed_out": bool, "refused": String} (see classify_key_reply); the key never appears in it.
- `func remember(key: String, day: int, data: Dictionary) -> void`
- `func lookup(key: String, day: int) -> Dictionary`
- `func count_source(source: String, n: int = 1) -> void`
- `func request_body(model: String, system_prompt: String, user_prompt: String, max_tokens: int) -> Dictionary`: The chat completion request for model: both prompts, its temperature (temperature_of, else TEMPERATURE), max_tokens and the model's MODEL_EXTRAS.
- `static func salvage_array(content: String) -> Dictionary`: Recovers the complete objects of a truncated {"key":[{...},{...},{... reply (GmiParse).
- `static func extract_json(content: String) -> Dictionary`: The JSON object in a model's reply: the largest valid one, whatever surrounds it (GmiParse).
- `func flush_cache() -> void`: Writes the recorded live responses so offline runs can replay real model output. Outside record mode the session file keeps each key's last 3 days (a pruned copy: session_cache itself stays whole, lookups read it) and is not rewritten when nothing was added since the last flush (the brain flushes at every day end). Record mode writes exactly as before.
- `func avg_latency_ms() -> int`
- `func to_dict() -> Dictionary`: The client's part of a save. The saved session cache keeps each key's last GmiCache. SAVE_KEEP_DAYS days (a lookup reads the nearest day, so older entries are never the answer once newer ones exist) and, while recording, everything: the in-memory cache is never pruned. The brain saves the same dictionary under its own "client" key.
- `func from_dict(d: Dictionary) -> void`

## `scripts/ai/gmi_image_client.gd`

class_name `GmiImageClient` · extends `Node`

Async poster image client for GMI's hy-image-v3.5-preview (slice D). request() returns a cache key at once; the texture arrives later through image_ready, always emitted deferred. Lookup order: memory LRU, user://posters/<key>.webp, the pre-baked set (exact key), the live queue (budgeted, breaker-guarded, never in GRIDFALL_OFFLINE), then the pre-baked pool of the kind and a procedural gradient. While a live image is on the way the request also gets a provisional texture (meta.provisional). Every wait reads `clock` and advances in tick(), so tests run on virtual time. Image processing runs on one background thread (poster_worker.gd). The API key never appears in any printed, stored or saved string.

### Signals

- `image_ready(key: String, tex: Texture2D, meta: Dictionary)`
- `image_failed(key: String, reason: String)`

### Constants

- `QUEUE_URL = "https://console.gmicloud.ai/api/v1/ie/requestqueue/apikey/requests"`
- `MODEL = "hy-image-v3.5-preview"`
- `STYLE_VERSION = "fp1"`
- `CACHE_DIR = "user://posters/"`
- `INDEX_PATH = "user://posters/index.json"`
- `MANIFEST_PATH = "res://assets/posters/manifest.json"`
- `PREBAKED_DIR = "res://assets/posters/"`
- `ART = preload("res://scripts/fp/posters/poster_art.gd")`
- `WORKER = preload("res://scripts/fp/posters/poster_worker.gd")`
- `WebSupport = preload("res://scripts/ops/web_support.gd")`
- `LRU_SIZE = 32`: Resident textures in the memory cache.
- `DAY_CAP = 6`: D12 budgets.
- `SESSION_CAP = 30`
- `MAX_IN_FLIGHT = 2`
- `BREAKER_FAILS = 3`
- `DISK_CAP = 400`: Kept files in user://posters before the oldest are deleted.
- `DOWNLOAD_LIMIT = 12 * 1024 * 1024`
- `POST_TIMEOUT_S = 120.0`
- `POLL_TIMEOUT_S = 30.0`
- `DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_S = 90.0`
- `SERVES_PER_TICK = 3`: Cache, disk and pre-baked serves handled per tick (each is one small load or a worker start).

### Properties

- `transport: Callable`: (method: String, url: String, headers: PackedStringArray, body: String, to_file: String) -> {"code": int, "body": PackedByteArray}. May be a coroutine. Default: one HTTPRequest per call.
- `allow_live_with_injected_transport: bool`: Test hook: honour the live path under GRIDFALL_OFFLINE=1, but only while `transport` is not the default HTTPRequest transport (an injected fake). The env check stays for the default transport.
- `clock: Callable`: Virtual clock in milliseconds; default Time.get_ticks_msec. Every wait below reads it.
- `player_pos: Callable`: () -> Vector3: the player's feet, which orders the live queue (ctx.player_position).
- `backoff_s: Array`: first and maximum 429 back-off
- `last_error: String`: The last failure, at most 140 characters of the server's body, scrubbed of the key.
- `transport_calls: int`: Transport calls made (tests), and real HTTPRequests the default transport started.
- `peak_in_flight: int`: Highest number of live jobs in flight at once (tests).

### Functions

- `func setup(client: GmiClient, day_fn: Callable) -> void`: client supplies api_key and live_enabled (read only); day_fn returns the current game day (sim.day), which drives the per-day cap and the breaker reset.
- `func close() -> void`: Stops every job (pending results are dropped) and joins the processing thread.
- `static func key_for(prompt: String, size: String) -> String`: Cache key of a prompt: sha256(MODEL|size|STYLE_VERSION|normalized prompt), 32 hex characters. Normalized: trimmed, lower case, runs of whitespace collapsed to one space.
- `func request(kind: String, prompt: String, size: String = "1536x640", priority: int = 0, pos: Vector3 = Vector3.INF) ->`: Returns the cache key immediately. The texture arrives through image_ready, which (like image_failed) is ALWAYS emitted with call_deferred, never inside request(). pos (world) orders the live queue by distance to the player; Vector3.INF means "no position". An empty prompt never goes live (a key restored from a save whose prompt is unknown).
- `func request_key(key: String, kind: String, size: String) -> String`: Like request(), for a key whose prompt is unknown: cache, disk, pre-baked or fallback, never live.
- `func get_cached(key: String) -> Texture2D`: Memory LRU or the user:// file (decoded on this thread), else null.
- `func budget_left_today() -> int`: Live images still allowed today (also bounded by the session cap and what is queued).
- `func in_flight() -> int`: Live jobs submitted and not finished.
- `func queued() -> int`: Live jobs waiting for a submit slot.
- `func breaker_open() -> bool`: True while the failure breaker blocks the live path.
- `func fallback_texture(kind: String, key: String, meta: Dictionary = {}) -> Texture2D`: A pre-baked or procedural texture for kind, picked deterministically by key (never live, never null). meta gets "source" and, for a pre-baked pick, "file".
- `func pool_files(kind: String) -> Array`: The pre-baked files that serve kind (its pool, else its family), sorted.
- `func tick(_dt: float) -> void`: Advances polling, back-off and submit spacing; _process calls tick(delta), tests call it directly.
- `static func long_edge(kind: String, size: String) -> int`: Long edge in pixels for a processed image: 1024 for wide (billboard, hoarding) art and the Gazette, 512 for portrait ads, walls and notices.
- `static func wants_vram_compress() -> bool`: VRAM compression only where a real device exists: on Compatibility GL and headless there is no main RenderingDevice, and the first S3TC compress spins Betsy up on the worker thread behind a half-initialised RenderingDevice singleton that the main thread's viewport configure then dereferences (engine bug, GL SIGSEGV, fault 0x8). Without a device the image stays RGB8 with mipmaps. Main thread only (RenderingServer is not worker-thread safe). Only the editor build carries the runtime BC compressor: an exported Linux or Windows build logs `_image_compress_bc_func is null` on every Image.compress call (an error burst per live poster) and keeps the image uncompressed anyway, so skip the call there.
- `static func wants_http_threads() -> bool`: Threaded (streaming) HTTPRequest downloads are not available on the web export: setting use_threads there freezes the browser, even on a threaded web build where threads_supported() answers true. Keep the worker-thread download to the desktop; every web build streams inline.
- `static func http_threads_for(threads: bool, web: bool) -> bool`: Pure form of wants_http_threads() so the web branch is testable without a web build.
- `func reset_pack_caches() -> void`: Posters pack arrived on a split web build: the manifest may have been read before its files existed. Forget it (and the textures that cached a miss) so the next lookup re-reads it.

## `scripts/ai/gmi_parse.gd`

class_name `GmiParse` · extends `RefCounted`

Reads the JSON object a model put in its reply. Models wrap it in prose, code fences or a <think> block, leave a trailing comma, write NaN, stop mid-sentence at the token limit, or answer only in their reasoning field. Every function is static and pure (no node, no network), so tools/tests/gmi_parse_test.gd can run a table of sample replies offline. extract_json() finds every balanced top-level {...} in the reply (string-aware, so a brace inside a quoted value does not count), repairs each (trailing commas, NaN and Infinity) and returns the largest one that parses as an object; the first wins a tie. A reply cut off by the token limit has no balanced object: it is closed at the last complete value instead, so what the model did finish is kept: its root-level members and the finished items of its lists (an order that has a nested object or list of its own is cut with that order, so no order is ever half made). When the cut falls before the first finished item of the list it was writing (a mayor stopped inside its first order), nothing is kept: the caller falls back as for any reply with no answer, instead of playing an idle day. A bare array reply ([{...}, {...}]) has no answer object, so it is {}. {} means there was no answer to be found.

### Constants

- `MAX_SCAN = 60000`: Longest reply scanned, in characters. A model that loops never makes the scan unbounded.
- `MAX_STARTS = 32`: Most "{" starting points tried and most candidate objects parsed from one reply.
- `MAX_CANDIDATES = 256`
- `MAX_UNCLOSED = 40`: A reply with more "{" than "}" by this much is not an answer (a reply cut off mid-way is a few levels short): {} at once, so a looping model cannot make the scan expensive.
- `MAX_REPAIRS = 4`: Unbalanced starts a truncation repair is tried from.
- `THINK_OPEN = "<think>"`
- `THINK_CLOSE = "</think>"`
- `LBRACE = 0x7B`: The characters the scans look at, as code points (cheaper than slicing a string per character).
- `RBRACE = 0x7D`
- `LBRACKET = 0x5B`
- `RBRACKET = 0x5D`
- `QUOTE = 0x22`
- `BACKSLASH = 0x5C`
- `COMMA = 0x2C`

### Functions

- `static func extract_json(content: String) -> Dictionary`: The object the reply carries: the largest valid balanced one, else a truncated reply closed at its last complete value, else {}. Never fails and never prints.
- `static func extract_json_info(content: String) -> Dictionary`: extract_json with how it got there: {"data": the object ({} when none), "truncated": true when the object is a cut-off reply closed at its last complete value}. One scan, so the caller that wants to count repairs (GmiReply) pays nothing extra.
- `static func visible_text(content: String) -> String`: The reply without its reasoning (what extract_json scans): <think> blocks cut out, the scan limit applied.
- `static func used_reasoning(msg: Dictionary) -> bool`: True when the reply put its answer in the reasoning field because its content was empty (message_text takes that way out).
- `static func message_of(choice: Variant) -> Dictionary`: The "message" of one entry of a reply's "choices" ({} when it is not an object holding one).
- `static func message_text(msg: Dictionary) -> String`: The reply's answer text for a chat message: its content (a string, or a list of parts with a "text"), and when that is empty the reasoning field some providers answer in. "" when none.
- `static func parse_object(text: String) -> Dictionary`: The object a JSON text parses to after the small repairs models need, or {} when it is not an object. Never prints (JSON.parse_string would log a parse error; a JSON instance does not).
- `static func repair(text: String) -> String`: text with trailing commas dropped and the bare NaN, Infinity and -Infinity tokens (JSON has no way to write them) turned into null. Quoted text is left alone.
- `static func salvage_array(content: String) -> Dictionary`: Recovers the complete objects of a truncated {"key":[{...},{...},{... reply. It is the fallback for a reply extract_json found nothing in.

## `scripts/ai/gmi_preflight.gd`

class_name `GmiPreflight` · extends `RefCounted`

The readiness check of a key (flag gmi_preflight): once per key, one GET of the model list through GmiClient (its own _models_trip, so no request leaves the process any other way), compared with the model ids the game calls (GmiReadiness), a sentence for the key panel and one line in the GMI log. The check goes out with the web-safe header set (Authorization and Content-Type only, whatever the build), is not retried, and leaves the client's breakers, live_outcomes and counters alone like the key test does. It starts by itself when a key is set (GmiClient.set_player_key calls key_changed) and at boot (Main calls run), but only where the game runs: `enabled` is Main's switch, so a test client never reaches for the network. It never asks without a key, under GRIDFALL_OFFLINE=1 or with the gmi_live kill switch off (GmiClient.test_refusal). The report holds model ids and counts, never the key.

### Signals

- `changed(report: Dictionary)`: The check of the key in use finished, or its report was cleared (a new key).

### Properties

- `enabled: bool`: Main sets this where the game runs; a test turns it on to test the check itself.
- `report: Dictionary`: The latest report of the key in use: {"ok", "total", "available", "missing", "offline", "skipped", "listed", "seconds"}, or {"ok": false, "error", "seconds"}; {} before one.

### Functions

- `func line() -> String`: The key panel's sentence for the latest report ("" before one): see GmiReadiness.line.
- `func key_changed(client: GmiClient) -> void`: The key in use changed: show the report of that key (none yet clears the line) and, where the game runs, start its check. Not awaited: the check finishes on its own.
- `func run(client: GmiClient, force: bool = false) -> Dictionary`: Asks for the model list of the key in use and returns the report. {} when the check was not made (not enabled, the flag off, no key, offline, the live kill switch), is still out for this key, or the key changed while it was out. The same key is asked once; force asks again.
- `static func fingerprint(key: String) -> String`: A short stand-in for a key, for telling keys apart without keeping one.
- `static func console_line(got: Dictionary, key: String) -> String`: The scrubbed console line of a finished check: counts and seconds only.

## `scripts/ai/gmi_readiness.gd`

class_name `GmiReadiness` · extends `RefCounted`

"Which of the 14 models does this key reach?" Pure helpers for GmiClient.preflight.run(): the list of model ids the game is configured to call (mayors, support agents, the resident and chatter pools), the ids a GET /v1/models reply names, their comparison, and the sentence the key panel shows. Nothing here touches the network or a node, so tools/tests/fp_gmi_ready_test.gd runs it with canned replies. What a missing model means: a mayor or a support agent whose model is missing plays from the recorded days or the scripted planner ("will use the offline planner"). A model of the resident or chatter pool is skipped: those callers rotate to another model after a few failures.

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`

### Functions

- `static func configured() -> Array[Dictionary]`: Every distinct model id the game calls, in a stable order, each with who uses it: [{"id", "users": [{"kind": "mayor" | "agent" | "pool", "name"}]}].
- `static func total() -> int`: How many distinct models the game calls (14 today).
- `static func ids_from_body(text: String) -> Array[String]`: The model ids a GET /v1/models reply names: the "id" (or the string itself) of each entry of its "data" or "models" list, or of a bare list. [] when the text is not such a reply.
- `static func compare(listed: Array) -> Dictionary`: Compares the ids a reply named with the configured ones: {"total", "available", "missing" (ids), "offline" (names of the mayors and agents that will use the offline planner), "skipped" (how many missing models belong only to the resident and chatter pools), "listed" (ids in the reply)}. Ids match without regard to case.
- `static func from_trip(trip: Dictionary, timeout_s: float) -> Dictionary`: The report for what GmiClient._models_trip returned ({"start_error": int}, or {"result", "http", "headers", "body"}): compare()'s result plus "ok" true, or {"ok": false, "error": a few words}. Never any text of the reply (an error body can echo the key). timeout_s is only worded.
- `static func line(report: Dictionary) -> String`: The sentence for a finished check. report is compare()'s result with "ok" and, when the check failed, "error" (a few words). "" for an empty report.

## `scripts/ai/gmi_reply.gd`

class_name `GmiReply` · extends `RefCounted`

Reads one chat-completion body into what the game keeps of it: the answer object, the text it came from, which repairs the reply needed, and what the API reported about its size. Pure and static (no node, no network), so tools/tests/ai_ledger_test.gd can feed it fenced, think-tagged and cut-off replies; GmiClient._post is the only caller in the game. Repairs name what GmiParse had to do to get an object out of the text (the ModelLedger counts them per model: they are the visible difference between hybrid-reasoning models): think_tag       a <think> block (or a lone </think>) was cut out fenced          the object came in a code fence trailing_comma  a trailing comma, NaN or Infinity had to be fixed (GmiParse.repair) salvaged        the reply was cut off by the token limit and closed at its last complete value reasoning_only  the content was empty and the answer was read from the reasoning field

### Constants

- `THINK_TAG = "think_tag"`
- `FENCED = "fenced"`
- `TRAILING_COMMA = "trailing_comma"`
- `SALVAGED = "salvaged"`
- `REASONING_ONLY = "reasoning_only"`
- `KINDS = [THINK_TAG, FENCED, TRAILING_COMMA, SALVAGED, REASONING_ONLY]`

### Properties

- `repair_scans: int`: How many times the full repair scan ran (a reply with a comma, NaN or Infinity candidate): a clean reply must leave it alone, which ai_ledger_test asserts (the scan is a script loop).

### Functions

- `static func read(body: Dictionary) -> Dictionary`: body: the parsed JSON of a 200 reply. Returns {"error": "" | "no choices", "data": {} (empty when the text held no object), "raw": the answer text, "repairs": Array of KINDS names (only when an object was found), "tokens_in", "tokens_out" (-1 when the API sent no usage), "finish_reason" ("" when absent)}.
- `static func classify(content: String, from_reasoning: bool, salvaged: bool) -> Array`: Which repairs reading content took (KINDS names, in KINDS order). from_reasoning: the text came from the reasoning field; salvaged: the object was recovered from a cut-off reply. Every reply passes through here, so a clean one costs a few native string searches and one regex scan, not a script loop (the loop in GmiParse.repair only runs when the regex saw a candidate).
- `static func usage_of(body: Dictionary, choice: Variant) -> Dictionary`: {"tokens_in", "tokens_out", "finish_reason"} from a reply body and its first choice: the usage counts (-1 when missing or not a number) and the reason the model stopped ("length" = it hit max_tokens).

## `scripts/ai/mayor_context.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Mayor context v2 (flag mayor_context_v2, default off until it has been tried live): what lets the five models answer EACH OTHER instead of five separate cities. A mayor's turn prompt gains the council's last ruling, the Grid Operator's order, the Chaos Director's strike, the league rank and the notes and requests other mayors left; its reply may carry vote_notes (why it voted so), message_to (one note a day to one mayor) and request (ask a mayor for money, answered by the existing grant action). Everything a model is asked to answer with is an id (argon ...): the prompt carries a table from the display names the other lines use to the ids, and a reply naming a mayor by display name or surname is understood too. With the flag off nothing here changes a prompt, a reply or a save. Offline planners and the replay cache never write notes, so notes exist only when a live model wrote them. Pure text and plain dictionaries: no nodes, no randomness, nothing new in the sim (a request is answered by the sim's own grant rule).

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `CouncilLog = preload("res://scripts/ai/council_log.gd")`
- `FLAG = "mayor_context_v2"`
- `VOTE_NOTE_CHARS = 60`
- `NOTE_CHARS = 120`
- `REASON_CHARS = 80`
- `REQUEST_MAX = 3000`: The most a request may ask for; the asked mayor's own treasury still limits the grant.
- `NOTES_PER_MAYOR = 4`: Notes kept per mayor, the days an unseen note stays worth showing, and the days a note is kept.
- `SHOW_DAYS = 3`
- `KEEP_DAYS = 8`
- `COUNCIL_DAYS = 4`: How long the last ruling, order and strike stay in a prompt (game days).
- `OPERATOR_DAYS = 6`
- `CHAOS_DAYS = 5`
- `CATEGORY = 25.0`: The league score of the street's table (ReporterDesk.CATEGORY): 25 points per category.
- `IDS = "argon|deepseek|kimi|qwen|grok"`
- `EXTRA_RULES = ("""    - A grant is sensible when a mayor asks, the need is real and you can still kee...`
- `ROSTER_HEAD = ('MAYOR IDS (answer fields such as grant "to", message_to "mayor" and ' + 'request "fro...`
- `REQUEST_LINE = 'REQUEST FROM %s (day %d): asks you for $%d - "%s". '`
- `REQUEST_PAY = ('To agree, add {"type":"grant","to":"%s","amount":%d} to your actions; you hold $%d an...`
- `REQUEST_SHORT = ('You hold $%d, less than they ask: you could grant at most that, {"type":"grant","to":...`
- `REQUEST_BROKE = "You have no funds to give, so you can only decline."`
- `SCHEMA_OLD = '"votes":{"ordinance_key":"yes or no"}}'`
- `SCHEMA_NEW = ('"votes":{"ordinance_key":"yes or no"},"vote_notes":{"ordinance_key":"<=60 chars"},' +...`
- `SPACES = [ "\n", "\r", "\t", "\u000b", "\u000c", "\u0085", "\u2028", "\u2029", "\u200b", "\u200c...`: What must not survive in a note: line and paragraph breaks, tabs and invisible spaces.
- `ORDINALS = ["1st", "2nd", "3rd", "4th", "5th"]`

### Functions

- `static func enabled() -> bool`
- `static func extend_system(text: String) -> String`: The system prompt with the optional fields and the grant guidance (unchanged with the flag off).
- `static func mayor_id(v: Variant) -> String`: The id (argon ...) of the mayor a model named by id, display name ("Viktor Han"), first name, surname or brand, with or without "Mayor"; "" when it names none.
- `static func display_of(mayor: String) -> String`: The display name of mayor id ("" for an unknown id).
- `static func clean_text(t: String, n: int) -> String`: Free text a model wrote, safe to show and to feed back into a prompt: no brand names (the display name stands in for a brand, whole-word ids included), one plain line (every kind of line break, tab and invisible space becomes a space, double quotes become single ones so the text cannot close the quotes the prompt wraps it in) and at most n characters, cut at a word.
- `static func fix_order(a: Dictionary) -> Dictionary`: An order with a grant's "to" turned into an id when the model wrote a name (flag on only).
- `static func roster_line() -> String`
- `static func user_lines(brain: CityBrain, mi: int, day: int) -> Array[String]`: The lines mayor mi's user prompt gains (empty with the flag off). Each appears only when the state it reports exists; all text about other agents is de-branded.
- `static func league_rows(sim: CitySim) -> Array[Dictionary]`: The street's league (people, jobs, approval, funds against the best mayor), best first: rows of {"mi", "pop", "jobs", "funds", "approval", "score"}. The same rule as ReporterDesk.standings, kept here because scripts/ai may not import the street's code.
- `static func league_line(sim: CitySim, mi: int) -> String`: "LEAGUE: you are 3rd of 5 (gaps to Duke Granger in 1st: people -120, ...)" for mayor mi; "" while nobody lives in the city yet. The leader sees the gap to the runner-up instead.
- `static func note_lines(brain: CityBrain, mi: int, day: int) -> Array[String]`: The notes and requests mayor mi has not read yet (and that are recent), as prompt lines.
- `static func unseen(brain: CityBrain, mayor: String, day: int) -> Array[Dictionary]`: Recipient's notes that were never shown and are at most SHOW_DAYS old, oldest first.
- `static func mark_seen(shown: Array[Dictionary], source: String) -> void`: Marks the notes a prompt showed (what unseen() returned when it was built) as read, but only when a model really answered that prompt (source "live"): if the call failed and the offline planner answered, nobody read them and they are shown again next turn. The builder itself changes nothing, so "Ask the five" can reuse it.
- `static func absorb(brain: CityBrain, mi: int, day: int, data: Dictionary, entry: Dictionary) -> void`: What a live reply adds to the world: vote_notes, one message_to and one request. entry is the turn's log entry (its "votes" are the votes that counted); stored fields land on it so the HUDs and the street feed can show them. Nothing here touches the sim: a request is answered, if at all, by the asked mayor's own grant order on a later turn.
- `static func prune(notes: Dictionary, day: int) -> void`: Drops notes older than KEEP_DAYS in place.
- `static func restore(raw: Variant) -> Dictionary`: A saved notes dictionary made safe to load: known mayors only, at most NOTES_PER_MAYOR each, text de-branded and cut again (a save is a file anyone can edit).

## `scripts/ai/mayor_prompts.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

The mayors' turn prompts, moved out of CityBrain (which keeps thin wrappers). system() is the rules and the reply schema, user() the day's state for one mayor. With the mayor_context_v2 flag off the text is exactly what CityBrain built before the move (a golden test pins it); with it on, MayorContext adds the council, operator, chaos and league lines, the notes between mayors and the extra reply fields. Pure reads: nothing here changes the brain or the sim.

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `MayorContext = preload("res://scripts/ai/mayor_context.gd")`
- `ANNEX_HEAD = ("LAND YOU CAN ANNEX (top-left x,y of each 16x16 plot, " + "price, open/forest/water ti...`

### Functions

- `static func system(mi: int) -> String`: The system prompt for mayor mi: persona, rules, actions and the reply schema.
- `static func user(brain: CityBrain, mi: int, day: int) -> String`: The user prompt for mayor mi on day: their district, the city, what the others said and decided.

## `scripts/ai/mayor_turns.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Staggered mayor turns (CityBrain.stagger_mayors, on in street mode). Instead of all five mayors deciding at dawn, they take the day's turns one by one, spread over the first SPAN of the day in an order that rotates daily, so a player on foot sees decisions land every few minutes. A turn still waiting when the day ends runs then (CityBrain._on_day_ended). No nodes.

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `SPAN = 0.9`: Share of the day the turns are spread over.

### Properties

- `due: Array[int]`: Mayors still to take the day's turn, in turn order.
- `day: int`: The day the waiting turns belong to.
- `opening: bool`: Armed by Main for a fresh street city (flag first_day_opening): day 1's turns use the compressed founding schedule (SimDefs.FIRST_DAY_START and FIRST_DAY_SPAN) instead of spreading over SPAN of the whole day. Not saved: a loaded city runs the ordinary schedule. clear() disarms it.

### Functions

- `func start(p_day: int, staggered: bool) -> bool`: Starts p_day: queues every mayor's turn when staggered. Returns staggered; false leaves the queue empty for the brain to run the mayors at dawn.
- `func take_due(progress: float, staggered: bool, busy: Array = []) -> int`: The mayor whose turn has come at progress (0..1 through the day), taken off the queue, or -1. Not staggered (street mode left mid-day), the next waiting mayor goes at once. A mayor still deciding (busy[mi], e.g. a live call from the day before) keeps the turn and holds the queue.
- `func take_all(busy: Array = []) -> Array[int]`: Every waiting turn whose mayor is free, taken off the queue (the day is ending). A mayor still deciding (busy[mi]) keeps the turn.
- `func next_turn() -> Dictionary`: The next turn: {"mi": mayor index, "at": the day fraction it starts}, or {} when nobody waits.
- `func clear() -> void`
- `func to_dict() -> Dictionary`
- `func from_dict(d: Variant) -> void`: Restores a saved queue; unknown or repeated mayor indices are dropped.
- `static func order(p_day: int) -> Array[int]`: The order of p_day's turns, rotated daily so nobody always goes first.
- `func turn_at(k: int) -> float`: The day fraction at which the k-th turn of the queue now running starts: the compressed founding schedule on an opening day 1, else at(k).
- `static func at(k: int) -> float`: The day fraction at which the k-th turn starts.
- `static func sim_idle(sim: Object) -> bool`: True while sim has no sliced job or spread work in flight (always for a synchronous sim). A staggered turn starts only then: its actions come from outside any job, and a mutator from outside finishes the job in flight, and the spread work it waits for, in that one frame.

## `scripts/ai/model_ledger.gd`

class_name `ModelLedger` · extends `RefCounted`

What each model has done in this city: calls, how many answered live, failed, fell back to a recorded answer or to the scripted planner, how long they took to answer, which errors they got, which repairs their replies needed, how many tokens they used and, for the mayors, how many of their orders the city accepted. It is the one place the street league, the orbit Arena tab and the "Services & minds" page read; nothing here draws. It is fed by two things only: GmiClient.call_logged / call_skipped (attach) for the calls, and CityBrain.mayor_decided (note_turn) for the orders. It lives in memory, owned by the brain (brain.ledger), and a save keeps a bounded copy (to_dict). Flag model_ledger turns it all off. Reading the numbers honestly: - "time to answer" is the call's latency_ms, which covers retries, back-off and waiting behind the other calls in flight: it is how long the city waited, not how fast the model is. - A mayor answers once a game day, so its p50 and p95 rest on a handful of calls: rows carry n_live, and p95 is only reported from P95_MIN_CALLS live answers on (-1 before). - replay and fallback count answers that did not come live (a recorded answer, the scripted planner after a failed or skipped call); a call whose live attempt failed and was then replayed counts in both live_fail and replay. - Accept% is the share of a mayor's orders the sim carried out, counted from this ledger's start (a save from before the ledger starts at zero). It covers live and replayed turns, because the sim validates every order whoever wrote it; the scripted planner's orders (a failed or skipped call) are not counted, they are not the model's. A replayed day may also carry up to two orders the replay top-up borrowed from the planner (CityBrain._replay_top_up).

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `MAX_EVENTS = 400`: Events kept for a timeline; a save keeps the newest SAVED_EVENTS of them.
- `SAVED_EVENTS = 40`
- `LAT_KEEP = 50`: Live answer times kept per model (the newest), for p50 and p95.
- `RECENT_KEEP = 8`: Outcomes kept for the health light.
- `MAX_MODELS = 48`
- `MAX_ERROR_CLASSES = 12`
- `P95_MIN_CALLS = 5`: Live answers a p95 needs before it means anything.
- `SLOW_MS = 30000`: A p95 time to answer slower than this (ms) makes the light amber.
- `SAVE_VERSION = 1`
- `OUT_OK = 0`: Outcome codes in a stat's "recent": answered live clean, answered live with a repair or a retry, failed.
- `OUT_WARN = 1`
- `OUT_FAIL = 2`
- `SKIPS = ["offline", "circuit open", "no free slot"]`: Errors that mean the call never went out (not a failed attempt).
- `ROLE_NAMES = { "residents": "Residents", "chatter": "Chat", "talk": "Talk", }`

### Properties

- `revision: int`: Bumped on every note: a view compares it with the one it drew to know it is stale.
- `models: Dictionary`: model id -> stat dict (see _new_stat); "mayor:<id>" -> the same for one mayor's own calls.
- `svc: Dictionary`: model id -> stat dict of what the model did OUTSIDE the mayors' chairs (the support agents, the residents, the chat voices). A model can sit in a chair and hold a service job (one of the resident minds is a mayor's model): its service row must not carry the mayor's answers.
- `turns: Array[Dictionary]`: One per mayor index: {"live", "replay", "fallback", "offline" (turns by where the answer came from), "ok", "rejected" (orders), "mix" (order type -> count)}.

### Functions

- `static func enabled() -> bool`: True unless the model_ledger flag is off.
- `func attach(client: GmiClient, reset: bool = false) -> void`: Starts listening to client's calls (and stops listening to the previous client's). reset true also forgets what was counted: a new city starts its own ledger.
- `func clear() -> void`: Forgets every count.
- `func note_call(rec: Dictionary) -> void`: One call (a GmiClient log record, slim or not): role, agent, model, source, latency_ms, attempts, error, tokens_in, tokens_out, finish_reason, repairs. A record without a model is ignored, and so is one of an isolated role (GmiClient.ISOLATED_ROLES: Ask the five): those calls promise to leave the breaker, the caches and the saves alone, and five parallel what-if answers would also skew the mayors' speed.
- `func note_turn(mi: int, entry: Dictionary) -> void`: One mayor's decided turn (the entry CityBrain.mayor_decided carries): where the answer came from and how the city took the orders.
- `func snapshot() -> Array[Dictionary]`: One row per model that made a call, busiest first: {"model", "label", "roles" (role -> calls), "calls", "live_ok", "live_fail", "replay", "fallback", "offline", "retries", "n_live", "last_ms", "mean_ms", "p50_ms", "p95_ms" (-1 when there is nothing to say), "errors" (class -> count), "repairs" (calls that needed one), "repair_kinds", "truncated" (cut off at max_tokens), "tokens_in", "tokens_out", "token_calls", "health"}. Orders and their accepted share are per mayor (mayor_rows): a model is not an order-giver.
- `func mayor_rows() -> Array[Dictionary]`: The five mayors in order: {"mi", "id", "who" (the person), "model" (the brand), "model_id", "label", "color"} plus the row fields of snapshot() for that mayor's own calls, "turns_live", "turns_replay", "turns_fallback", "turns_offline", "orders_ok", "orders_rejected", "accept_pct" (-1 before any order), "mix" (order type -> count) and "health".
- `func services() -> Array[Dictionary]`: One row per model the city uses outside the mayors' chairs (the support agents, the resident minds, the chat voices), known ones first even before they have made a call: {"model", "label", "kinds" (names of the jobs it has or is meant to have), "mix" ("Gazette 4 · Chat 9"), "calls" (outside the mayors), "live_ok", "live_fail", "replay", "fallback", "offline", "p50_ms", "health"}. A model is one row however many jobs it has.
- `static func roster() -> Array[Dictionary]`: The models the city is meant to run outside the mayors: [{"model", "name"}] for the six support agents, the resident minds and the chat voices.
- `func recent_events(n: int = 60) -> Array[Dictionary]`: The newest events, oldest first (at most n).
- `static func role_name(role: String) -> String`: A job's name as a viewer reads it: a support agent's own name, else ROLE_NAMES, else the role.
- `static func short_name(model_id: String) -> String`: The model id without its vendor and a trailing date stamp ("deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731" -> "DeepSeek-V4-Flash").
- `static func error_class(err: String) -> String`: The kind of failure an error text is: an HTTP code ("429"), "network", "no JSON", "bad reply", "skipped" (the call never went out) or "other"; "" for no error.
- `static func percentile(values: Array, p: float) -> int`: The p-th percentile (0..100, nearest rank) of values; -1 when there are none.
- `static func seconds_text(ms: int) -> String`: "11.2 s" for a time in ms; "-" for none.
- `static func health_of(st: Dictionary) -> String`: The health word for a stat dict: "idle" (no call yet), "grey" (nothing but replay and scripted answers: no live call to judge), "red" (the last two live calls failed), "amber" (a recent failure, repair or retry, or a p95 slower than SLOW_MS over at least P95_MIN_CALLS answers), else "green".
- `func to_dict() -> Dictionary`: A bounded copy for a save: every stat (their lists are capped), the five mayors' turn counts and the newest SAVED_EVENTS events (without their wall-clock stamp). A day of play adds nothing: it only moves the same numbers.
- `func from_dict(d: Dictionary) -> void`: Loads what to_dict wrote. Anything missing or of the wrong type is skipped: a save is a file anyone can edit.

## `scripts/ai/resident_minds.gd`

class_name `ResidentMinds` · extends `Node`

Gives every resident a GMI brain. Once a day residents are planned in batches of ten, each batch on a different fast model. When something breaks, the people near it and the people with the right trade are asked how they react. Every answer is cached per resident so offline runs replay what the real models decided; the heuristic below only covers residents nobody has met yet.

### Signals

- `plans_done(day: int)`
- `reacted(ev: Dictionary, responses: Array)`
- `busy_changed(n: int)`

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `MODELS = [ "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash", "google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite", "MiniMaxAI/MiniMax...`
- `BATCH = 10`
- `MAX_REACTORS = 10`
- `EFFECTS = { "fire": "a building is burning and the fire can spread to its neighbours", "blackout"...`
- `PLAN_SYSTEM = """`
- `REACT_SYSTEM = """`

### Functions

- `func setup(p_sim: CitySim, p_people: Residents, p_client: GmiClient, p_brain: Node) -> void`
- `func pending() -> int`
- `func plan_day(day: int) -> void`
- `func spreading() -> bool`: True while spread plan batches or reactions are still waiting for their frame (sliced mode).
- `func drain_step() -> void`: Runs the next waiting spread item (the drain scheduler's step; _run_spread does one a frame).
- `func finish_spread() -> void`: Runs every waiting spread item now (a save, skip or mode switch needs the whole day planned).
- `func to_dict() -> Dictionary`
- `func from_dict(d: Dictionary) -> void`

## `scripts/ai/road_plans.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

The heuristic mayor's road orders (CityBrain._heuristic_mayor): new roads to open land, at as cheap a grade as the funds call for, and paving rough roads that lots have grown along. Static, reads the sim only. No nodes.

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `PAVE_FUNDS = 9000`: A heuristic mayor with more than this to spend paves a rough road that lots have grown along.

### Functions

- `static func road_step(sim: CitySim, mi: int, open_lots: int, funds: int, actions: Array, notes: Array) -> void`: The day's road order for mayor mi, if any, appended to actions with a note: new road to open land when fewer than 6 lots are left, else paving a rough road beside built lots.
- `static func thrifty_grade(funds: int) -> String`: The road grade a heuristic mayor with funds to spare builds new roads at.
- `static func plan_paving(sim: CitySim, mi: int) -> Dictionary`: A paving order along an unpaved road tile with a built-up lot beside it: its straight run of unpaved tiles in the district, up to 12 long. Empty when there is none.
- `static func plan_road(sim: CitySim, mi: int) -> Dictionary`: A paved road order of up to 12 tiles across empty land in mi's district that starts or ends next to an existing road. Empty when there is none.
